title: NY State Assembly · District 60
area: Brooklyn, including Starrett City and East New York

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican/Conservative primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled; incumbent Nikki Lucas (D) and Norman Ramsay (R, Conservative) each advanced without appearing on a primary ballot.

candidates.name: Nikki Lucas
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 60 (since February 2022)

positions.summary: Sponsored a bill requiring firearm owners to carry at least $1 million in liability insurance.

record.text: Assigned to the Aging, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Energy, Health, Housing, and Labor committees (2023-2024 and 2025-2026 sessions).

Prime sponsor of A05603, the 'New York State American Freedmen Task Force on Reparations Remedies Act,' which would establish a state task force to examine and make determinations on reparations for descendants of American slavery; referred to committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.
Prime sponsor of A08284, the 'New York State Freedmen's Bureau Act,' which would create a state freedmen's bureau to administer reparations; referred to committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.
Prime sponsor of A05611, which would require firearm owners to carry at least $1 million in liability insurance; referred to the Insurance Committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

candidates.name: Norman Ramsay

priorities.text: "Our seniors built our communities. They deserve dignity, security, and protection."
"Protect the Home. Protect the Family. Protect the Future."

candidates.researchNotes: Ramsay completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey with brief campaign-message answers but did not take clear stances on this guide's fixed issue list, so no Position entries are included. No independent campaign website with additional policy detail could be located; the URL listed on his Ballotpedia profile (votesayf.com) now resolves to an unrelated musician's website and was not used as a source.
